headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0277 — SMTO can't type some of these characters on that computer

html:
SMTO-EXE-0277 — SMTO can't type some of these characters on that computer

GUID: be80e4dc-e571-557d-a3d1-f5c48026b197
Slug: ui-text-unrepresentable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The keyboard layout on the Gateway's Linux computer has no key for some characters SMTO needed to type, such as accented letters, symbols or emoji. SMTO didn't type any of the text.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway's computer, switch the keyboard back to its first (main) layout and leave it there while SMTO types. SMTO can type only with the first keyboard layout; another active layout stops it.
  2. Ask SMTO to fill in the field by its name instead of typing at a spot on the screen. Filling a field directly puts the text in without pressing individual keys.
  3. Or ask SMTO to put the text on that computer's clipboard and paste it, approving each step if SMTO asks. Pasting works for any character, but it replaces whatever was on that computer's clipboard.

What success looks like

  • The full text, including the special characters, appears correctly in the field.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer, noting which characters were involved.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Linux guarded typing preflight found a character with no keysym in the first two levels of the current core keymap, a non-zero active XKB layout group, missing libX11, or a keymap change before dispatch.

What this means

  • Native keyboard cannot represent the requested text. Use supported text or explicitly write the text with Clipboard and issue a guarded paste shortcut under existing permissions.

Why this can happen

  • Native keyboard cannot represent the requested text.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect fresh capture geometry, surface identity and focus.

How to fix it

  • Switch the X session to its first XKB layout group or a layout that contains the characters. Otherwise use semantic set_value or type_text on an accessibility element, or an authorized Clipboard write followed by a guarded paste shortcut, and report the clipboard change.
  • Use supported text or explicitly write the text with Clipboard and issue a guarded paste shortcut under existing permissions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use supported text or explicitly write the text with Clipboard and issue a guarded paste shortcut under existing permissions.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh evidence establishes the requested outcome.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
